project_scope.note: A. erecta remains the primary local research anchor; A. serpentaria supplies the current rights-cleared family visual.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Go straight to the flower: local Aristolochia has one fused petaloid perianth/calyx tube rather than a normal separate petal corolla.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate simple exstipulate leaves; shape varies from narrow in A. erecta to broader/cordate in other species.
family_diagnostics.flower: Often strongly zygomorphic; petaloid fused calyx/perianth, petals absent in Aristolochia.
family_diagnostics.ovary: Inferior; anthers are closely associated with the stylar column/gynostemium.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Do not require a giant Dutchman's-pipe vine—A. erecta is a small erect/sprawling perennial.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Aristolochiaceae is a flower-architecture family: the strange tube is the perianth/calyx, not an ordinary corolla of petals.

steps.title: 1 · See the family habit range
steps.look_for: A small herbaceous Aristolochia rather than a huge tropical pipevine.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the learner from making vine habit mandatory.

steps.title: 2 · Learn the flower plan
steps.look_for: A single curved petaloid perianth tube rather than separate petals.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest family-level mental model.

steps.title: 3 · Put the ovary below the tube
steps.look_for: The ovary positioned below the perianth and the compact reproductive column inside.
steps.why_it_matters: Inferior ovary + gynostemium separates Aristolochia from many fused-flower vines.

steps.title: 4 · Return to the local swanflower
steps.look_for: Narrow grass-like leaves and a much smaller brown-purple tubular flower.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the actual Central Texas field form to expect.

comparisons.title: Aristolochiaceae vs Apocynaceae
comparisons.rule: Apocynaceae has a true fused corolla and usually superior ovary; Aristolochia uses a petaloid fused calyx/perianth and inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Aristolochiaceae vs Convolvulaceae
comparisons.rule: Morning-glories have a plicate corolla and superior ovary; Aristolochia has the peculiar perianth tube and inferior ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: The current reference image is A. serpentaria; an exact rights-cleared A. erecta flower macro remains a future photo lock.
